title: FHR: FAIR Header Reference genome (FAIR-bioHeaders), plus the gtars RefgetStore sidecar variant
maintainer: FAIR-bioHeaders project (David Molik and Adam Wright hold schema authority); sidecar variant: databio (gtars) and refgenie

formats.description: FHR metadata as a standalone JSON file (FHR 2.1; the same shape holds FHR 1 and 2.0 records)
formats.record_key: checksum (when it is the real file checksum); otherwise none: a standalone metadata file has no identity of its own. seqcol_id identifies the collection.

formats.description: FHR metadata as a YAML file (YAML 1.2 core types that read the same under 1.1, rule R12)
FHR YAML embedded at the top of a FASTA file in ;~ comment lines; the checksum covers the whole file
formats.record_key: checksum (SHA-512/256 of the file bytes except the checksum line)

formats.description: FHR YAML embedded at the top of a GFA file in #~ comment lines; the checksum covers the whole file
formats.record_key: checksum (SHA-512/256 of the file bytes except the checksum line)

formats.description: FHR JSON-LD: the same record plus the FHR @context and @type keys (rules J1-J9); extension fields are not allowed
FHR metadata as HTML microdata (itemtype = raw-main fhr.json URL, data-fhr-type annotations, rules M1-M5); extension fields are not allowed
One-way schema.org export: the record split into typed nodes (assembly Dataset, metadata record, CreateAction, Observations, Grant, ScholarlyArticle) in an @graph; cannot be read back to FHR
RefgetStore FHR sidecar: gtars FhrMetadata serialized as JSON at <store>/fhr/<seqcol digest>.fhr.json (refgenie's public stores)
formats.record_key: seqcolDigest (the file name <seqcolDigest>.fhr.json; not in the JSON body), within one RefgetStore

fields.description: centralized schema file (the URL of the FHR schema this record follows)
fields.notes: Selects the schema version (SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md V1-V7): raw-main URL = current schema; w3id or raw tag URL = that release. Raw-main plus schemaVersion 1 means an FHR 1 record (V6).

fields.description: Version of the FHR schema contract, as "MAJOR.MINOR" ("2.0" or "2.1")
fields.notes: A string from v0.4 (FHR 2.0); the number 1 (often written 1.0) in FHR 1 / releases up to v0.3.1. Distinct from the assembly `version` and from the release tag.

fields.description: Name of the Genome
fields.notes: Free text. The upstream example uses a descriptive name; refgenie sidecars put a collection-style name here (hg38, sacCer3, R64-1-1), so in practice it may name a collection rather than the assembly.

fields.description: Other common names of the genome
fields.notes: List of strings. refgenie uses it for collection aliases (GRCh38, sacCer3-igenomes-ucsc).

fields.description: Species name (taxon.name)
fields.notes: taxon is required; a conforming record has a non-empty taxon.name or taxon.uri. A planned FHR 3.0 rule will require taxon.uri.

fields.description: URL of the species at identifiers.org (taxon.uri)
fields.notes: Pattern ^https://identifiers\.org/taxonomy:[0-9]+$ (NCBI Taxonomy id after the colon).

fields.description: Version number of Genome eg. 1.2.0
fields.notes: The assembly's own version, not schemaVersion. refgenie fills it with the number after the dot of the NCBI accession (GCA_000001405.15 -> "15").

fields.description: Author of the FHR instance (person or organization): name
fields.notes: Who wrote this metadata record, not the assembly. One list item per author, aligned with the other metadataAuthor[] lists; None where an author lacks the key. metadataAuthor itself is required; a conforming author has a non-empty name.

fields.description: Author of the FHR instance: ORCID URI
fields.notes: Pattern ^https://orcid\.org/NNNN-NNNN-NNNN-NNN[0-9X]$ (only ORCID is allowed in 2.x).

fields.description: Whether the author is a person (Personal) or an organization (Organizational), as DataCite nameType
fields.notes: Enum Personal|Organizational; added in v0.4 (FHR 2.0).

fields.description: Assembler of the Genome (person or org): name
fields.notes: assemblyAuthor itself is required; a conforming author has a non-empty name.

fields.description: Assembler of the Genome: ORCID URI
fields.notes: ORCID pattern, as for metadataAuthor.

fields.description: Personal or Organizational (DataCite nameType)
fields.notes: Enum; added in v0.4. Example value from conformance vector valid/jsonld-author-name-type.fhr.jsonld (not copied here).

fields.description: Date the genome assembly was created
fields.notes: ISO date (format: date). In YAML it must stay a string (rule R12).

fields.description: Description of the physical sample
fields.notes: Free text (was physicalSample in the 2022 FFRGS draft).

fields.description: Accession of the genome assembly (accessionID.name)
fields.notes: The schema description is garbled ("accessionID genome assembly was created"). The official example puts an institution name (PBARC) here; refgenie puts the INSDC assembly accession (GCA_000001405.15). Unique only within the database it comes from.

fields.description: URL of the accession record (accessionID.url)
fields.notes: refgenie writes https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/<accession>/.

fields.description: Physical tools and instruments used in the creation of the genome assembly
fields.notes: List of free-text instrument names.

fields.description: DOI (without a resolver prefix) of the scholarly article where the genome was published
fields.notes: Pattern ^10\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*/\S+$. FHR 1 allowed anything starting with 10.

fields.description: Documentation about the genome
fields.example: Synthetic metadata and sequence; identifiers are placeholders unless explicitly verified.
fields.notes: Free text describing the genome; refgenie uses it as the genome description. In JSON-LD a URL value is written as subjectOf.

fields.description: Identifiers of the genome as prefix:accession (CURIE-like)
fields.notes: Pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+:.+$. Which kind of identifier is not said; each is unique within its prefix.

fields.description: Related URLs to the genome
fields.notes: Any related URL; refgenie's hg38 sidecar lists a download URL of the FASTA (a copy) and a blog post.

fields.description: Grant line item
fields.notes: Free text; the schema.org export turns it into a Grant node.

fields.description: License and reuse conditions for the use of the Genome
fields.notes: Free text (the 2022 draft called it licence). gtars and the refgenie registry use a different key, license, which is not an FHR field.

fields.description: Masking applied to the genome assembly
fields.notes: Enum by pattern: not-masked|hard-masked|soft-masked|repeat-masked|unknown. A property of a particular FASTA file: soft-masking does not change refget digests (sequences are uppercased first), hard-masking does.

fields.description: Contig L50: the smallest number of contigs whose lengths sum to at least 50 percent of the assembly length
fields.notes: Computed over the sequences of the file; describes the assembly only when the file holds all of it.

fields.description: Contig N50: contig length in base pairs at 50 percent of the assembly length
Contig L90
Contig length in base pairs at 90 percent of the assembly length
fields.notes: Added in v0.3.

fields.description: Total base pairs of the genome assembly
Number of contigs of the genome assembly
Number of scaffolds of the genome assembly
Scaffold N50
fields.notes: Added in v0.4. No official example sets it.

fields.description: Scaffold N90
fields.notes: Added in v0.4. No official example sets it.

fields.description: Scaffold L50
fields.notes: Added in v0.4. No official example sets it.

fields.description: Scaffold L90
fields.notes: Added in v0.4. No official example sets it.

fields.description: GC content as a percentage (0 to 100), not a fraction
fields.notes: Added in v0.3.

fields.description: Read technology of the genome assembly (short, long, hifi, etc.)
fields.notes: Free text.

fields.description: SHA-512/256 of the file, standard padded base64 (44 characters)
fields.notes: Rules R1-R5: hash of the exact (decompressed) file bytes except the root checksum line, so metadata, comments and sequence all count. It identifies one exact FASTA/GFA file, not the sequences. Old FHR docs used md5: values; the refgenie registry writes sha256:<hex>, which is not FHR. In standalone JSON/YAML/JSON-LD/HTML examples it is a placeholder.

fields.description: Assembly software: legacy name string
fields.notes: assemblySoftware is either this legacy string or a list of objects (the assemblySoftware[] fields). Example value from conformance vector valid/jsonld-legacy-software-string.fhr.jsonld (not copied here); the 2022 draft example used HiFiASM.

fields.description: Assembly software name
fields.notes: Required in each software object.

fields.description: Assembly software URI
Assembly software version
Command-line arguments used
fields.notes: One list of argument strings per software item, so the value is a list of lists.

fields.description: URI of the assembly protocol or workflow documentation
fields.notes: Added in v0.3.

fields.description: Unprefixed GA4GH refget sequence collection top-level digest (sha512t24u); supplied by the user, not calculated by FHR
fields.notes: 32 base64url characters. The link from FHR to the seqcol level. Added in v0.3. Official examples hold a placeholder (all A); several FHR files (for example soft-masked and unmasked copies) can share one digest. The schema.org export writes it as identifier PropertyValue 'GA4GH refget sequence collection'. Example: the real hg38 digest, as used in the constructed anchors.

fields.description: Extension field (R15): who distributed this sequence set
fields.notes: The upstream example holds a placeholder. The constructed anchors move refgenie's assemblySource here (ncbi, Ensembl, UCSC; not normalized). Extension fields mean nothing to the standard.

fields.description: Extension field (R15): NCBI assembly level
fields.notes: Only in constructed anchors (refgenie's assemblyLevel moved to an x- key).

fields.description: Seqcol top-level digest of the collection this sidecar describes
fields.notes: NOT a key in the JSON body: gtars FhrMetadata.seqcol_digest is #[serde(skip)], and the store names the file <seqcolDigest>.fhr.json. read(text) cannot see it, so native records from read() never contain it; a caller that knows the file name can add it (fhr.sidecar_digest(filename)), and write() drops it. Example from examples/sidecar_hg38_jungle_EiFob05aCWgVU_B_Ae0cypnQut3cxUP1.fhr.json.
